title: Behold Thy Waiting Servant, Lord
description: Behold Thy Waiting Servant, Lord in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 119, part 10, headed “Pleading the promises”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold thy wait-ing ser-vant, Lord, De-vot-ed to thy fear; Re-mem-ber and con-firm thy word, For all my hopes are there.

lines: For all my hopes are there.
Hast thou not writ salvation down,
Doth not my heart address thy throne?
Mine eyes for thy salvation fail;
Nor let the scoffing lips prevail,
Didst thou not raise my faith, O Lord?
Saints shall rejoice in my reward,
And trust as well as fear.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
